$comment: Reviewer registry for the review-attestation gate (TOOL-021, #1140).
The gate asks ONE question: did a review actually happen? It never asks who
performed it or how good it was. A human review attests exactly as well as a
bot's.
This file exists so that answering that question does not require a code
change when the reviewer changes. Ported from mlorentedev/dotfiles
harness/review-attestation.json at 2bac1c5 (GUARD-002, #906), with the
values below measured against this repository rather than copied.
`declined_markers` are the strings identifying a reviewer's 'I could not
review' notice. Prefer an HTML comment marker over prose: prose is
translated, reworded and A/B tested, while the marker is machine output. If
a vendor changes it, the affected PR reads `pending` instead of `declined` —
still red, so marker drift degrades the MESSAGE and never the verdict.
`review_markers` identify a reviewer's comment-shaped review output, for a
reviewer that does not use the reviews API. Empty for a reviewer that files
proper reviews: an auto-summary comment is not a review and must not attest.
Logins are matched with a trailing `[bot]` stripped and case folded, because
the two GitHub APIs disagree: GraphQL returns `github-actions`, REST returns
`github-actions[bot]`. Matching the raw string would make the gate depend on
which API produced the payload.
Note what is NOT here: any notion of which models may review. That policy
lives in harness/reviewer-pool.json and governs the SPEC-level adversarial
review — a different gate with a different purpose, deliberately not merged
with this one.

reviewers.why: Per-account PR review limit, reached routinely because parallel sessions drain it. NOT a free-tier problem, and an earlier framing of #1140 said it was: the account is Pro Plus and CodeRabbit's own footer reads 'It's free for OSS'. Measured on #1155, where the notice rendered while `gh pr checks` reported `CodeRabbit  pass`. The marker is the HTML comment CodeRabbit emits around the notice, not its prose.

declined_markers: You have reached your Codex usage limits for code reviews
reviewers.why: The second autonomous reviewer on this repository, present on #1153, #1155 and #1156. On #1155 it and CodeRabbit were exhausted SIMULTANEOUSLY — two independent account-wide quotas, correlated because parallel sessions drain both, and neither notice blocked the merge. This entry is the reason #1140's framing had to widen: the defect is not one vendor's status lying, it is that every reviewer configured here fails open. Measured 2026-08-19: Codex emits NO HTML comment marker, so this one is prose against the registry's own preference. Accepted with the consequence stated — if the wording drifts the PR reads `pending` rather than `declined`, which is still red.

PR-Agent (TOOL-021 Part 2) posts as github-actions via GITHUB_TOKEN and publishes through the comments API, not the reviews API — so reviews[] is empty on a PR it genuinely reviewed. Declared ahead of Part 2 landing: the gate must not call this repository's own reviewer unreviewed the day it starts running. The marker is the `review` command's own heading; `## PR Code Suggestions` (the `improve` command) is deliberately NOT here — suggestions are not a review.

escape.label: merged-unreviewed
escape.why: Both are required, never one. Same shape as the spec gate's skip-sdd escape, chosen because it is already understood here and because it forces the disclosure into the durable record instead of a chat message. Proceeding on an unreviewed PR is allowed; proceeding SILENTLY is not.

signatures.name: release-please (api + errors)
signatures.why: A release PR restates commits already on master, each reviewed when it merged. Measured on #767, #806 and #842: exactly these five paths. Verified NOT author-matchable — the author reads `mlorentedev`, a human, because release-please runs under a PAT.

signatures.name: release-please (api only)
signatures.why: release-please opens PER-APP releases, so the file set VARIES and one signature is not enough. Measured on #804, which carried exactly these three. This is where the port had to diverge from upstream: matching is exact set equality in both directions, and upstream's own comment understates that as 'every changed file must appear in the declared set'. Under exact equality a single superset signature exempts #842 and REFUSES #804 — verified before writing this file. Enumerating each real shape keeps the strict semantics rather than relaxing them, and the strictness is the safe direction: adding a third app produces a red PR asking for a new signature, never a silent exemption.

signatures.name: release-please (errors only)
signatures.why: The third shape release-please can produce with the current two apps. Declared by construction rather than by measurement — unlike the other two it has not been observed, because errors has not yet released alone. Recorded as unobserved so nobody later reads it as evidence.
